text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parti Quebecois drops Ontario job barrier: Ontario threats lead to deal allowing construction workers across boundary.
- Bosnian factions keeping weapons: Bulk of arms in Serb hands.
- State-trooper look considered for police: All Ontario forces to wear same hats.
- Quebec's Liberals want changes to Constitution: Recognition of 'uniqueness' sought to counter separatists.
- Only one vote counts in Hong Kong race: One candidate is probably more equal than the others, thanks to the Beijing factor.
- Manulife strikes Altamira deal: Gets control as outraged key shareholder disputes pact's legality.
- Ottawa sidesteps trade spat with U.S.: Approves four audio licences, gains pledge from Shaw Communications to boost Canadian content.
- Finance Minister Paul Martin allows book tax rebates: But says three provinces must fund blended GST exemption.
- Optimism boosts dollar above C$0.74: Hits level for first time in a year.
- FBI sting operation nets Canadian CEO: Cam-Net Communications chief Daryl Buerge is one of 45 charged with with securities fraud after probe of illegal payments to U.S. brokers.
- Manulife takes a tenuous grip on Altamira.
